sentences.text: 14. In this regard, the filing of charge sheet in the Criminal case is prima-facie evidence for this case to prove that the accident was due to the rash and negligent driving of driver of Mahindra Bolero bearing reg.No.KA-11-A-7996.

In fact, the proof of accident itself is sufficient for the purpose of this case, as held by the Hon'ble Supreme Court in a decision reported in 2001 ACJ 1975 (Sri. Kumaresh V/s. The Divisional Manager, National Insurance Com. Ltd., and another)

It is sufficient, if it is established that the claimant has sustained injuries as a result of the accident.

In view of the ratio laid down by the Hon'ble Supreme Court in the above decision and also prima-facie evidence produced by 4801/2021 & 4847/2021 the petitioner, it is proved and established that the accident was occurred due to rash and negligent driving of driver of the offending vehicle and the deceased in all the cases died due to the injuries sustained in the RTA.

Further PW-4 clearly deposed that he has given statement before police and identified the accused and also identified vehicle Bolero pickup vehicle bearing reg.No.KA-11-A-7996.
Though PW-4 was cross examined at length by the respondent counsel, but nothing worth was elicited from the mouth of the PW-4.

Even in the cross examination, PW-4 clearly stated that he has seen the accident and further deposed that one Bolero pickup vehicle has hit to the deceased motor cycle, they have seen the Bolero pickup vehicle.

Thereafter Bolero pickup vehicle has ran away from 4801/2021 & 4847/2021 the spot and denied the suggestion made by the respondent counsel that the accident has been taken place due to rash and negligent driving of the deceased himself.

Thus from the evidence of the PW-4 eye witness and coupled with the police documents, it is clearly established the involvement of the Bolero vehicle in the accident and the accident has been taken place due to the rash and negligent driving of the driver of the Bolero vehicle.

"In a situation of this nature, the Tribunal has rightly taken a holistic view of the matter.
It was necessary to be borne in mind that strict proof of an accident caused by a particular bus in a particular manner may not be possible to be done by the claimants.
The claimants were merely to establish their case on the touchstone of preponderance of probability.
The standard of proof beyond reasonable doubt could not have been applied."
18. Thus, the oral evidence of PW-1 discussed with the above documentary evidence are sufficient for the purpose 4801/2021 & 4847/2021 of the actionable claim under the Motor Vehicles Act.
Mere taking of defence is not sufficient to dislodge the testimony of other side, which has no sanctity in the eyes of Law.
19. Under such circumstances the evidence of PW.1 which is supported by police documents has to be accepted.
Consequently I hold that the accident is proved to have been caused due to the actionable negligence of the driver of offending vehicle.

In view of the ratio laid down by the Hon'ble Apex Court in Civil Appeal No.79/2020 (Mohammad Siddique & another V/s National Insurance Company Ltd & others), such violation by itself, without anything more, cannot lead to a finding of contributory negligence.
Under such circumstances, contributory negligence cannot be attributed to the deceased.
Though the insurance company denied the cause of the accident as well as the very involvement of its insured vehicle, it has not let in any cogent evidence to this effect.
